description: Publish a recipe to Befana. When the cook pastes, types or links a recipe, call draft_recipe first, show them the draft and publish it here with create_recipe({ draft_id }) once they confirm: never publish their text straight from fields, even a short one (for a recipe card photo, read it and pass the text to draft_recipe). Pass fields without a draft_id only for a recipe you worked out with the cook in this conversation, after showing it to them. Write each step with ingredient tags instead of typed amounts: "Whisk {flour} with {salt}". Tags default to the last word of the ingredient name ("all-purpose flour" → {flour}); set key to choose. Use {butter:1/2} when an ingredient is split across steps and {t:375} for oven temperatures in °F. title, servings, ingredients and steps are required, unless you pass draft_id: then the draft from draft_recipe is published, with any fields you pass replacing the draft's. Publish a draft only after the cook has seen and confirmed it. Returns the url plus any warnings (e.g. an ingredient never used in a step). Recipes are public and appear under My recipes in the cook's kitchen. An exact copy of a recipe the cook already has is refused: change that one with update_recipe instead. tested marks it cooked and timed, only when the cook tells you they made it and how long it took; ask, never assume.

chef_note.description: The chef's note, up to 500 characters: a sentence or two in the cook's words on what makes the recipe theirs. Only what the cook said; never write one for them.

draft_id.description: A draft_id from draft_recipe, to publish that draft

key.description: Short tag steps use, e.g. "flour". When omitted: an ingredient already in the recipe keeps its key (match by item), a new one takes the tag your steps use for it if that tag is its name ("nutritional_yeast") or last word ("yeast"), else the last word of item.

qty.description: Amount, e.g. 1.5 or "1 1/2". Use 0 for 'to taste'.

unit.description: tsp, tbsp, cup, fl oz, qt, oz, lb, g, kg, ml, l, clove, can, slice, sprig, bunch, head, stick, each, or empty

body.description: Step text with amounts as tags: {flour}, a portion {butter:1/2}, oven temp in °F {t:375}

tip.description: A short pointer shown under the step, up to 140 characters: "The batter should look lumpy; don't overmix."

summary.description: One or two sentences on what makes it good

minutes.description: How long it took, start to finish, in minutes

tested.description: Mark the recipe tested: the cook says they cooked it themselves and timed it. Ask the cook ("Have you cooked this? About how long did it take, start to finish?") and pass only what they say; never assume it, never estimate the minutes, and never mark a recipe tested because you drafted, imported or adapted it. null clears the mark. Shown as "Tested by the cook · 45 min" and counted as one timed cook.

name: create_recipe
title: Publish a new recipe
